recipes.name: Murgh Makhani (Indian Butter Chicken)
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces

steps.text: Stir yogurt and tandoori masala powder in a large bowl until combined; add chicken and toss to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour. Drain and discard excess marinade.
Puree onion, ginger, water, and garlic in a blender until it forms a smooth paste; set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chicken and cook until lightly brown, about 5 minutes. Remove from the skillet and set aside.

Heat remaining 2 tablespoons oil in the same skillet. Fry onion paste until moisture is mostly evaporated, about 3 minutes. Sprinkle garam masala and chili powder over mixture; cook for 1 minute more. Add tomato sauce, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook another 5 minutes.

Return chicken to the skillet. Add half-and-half and bring to a boil. Add butter, fenugreek leaves, and salt; reduce heat to low and simmer, uncovered, until chicken is no longer pink in the middle, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Murgh Makhani (Indian Butter Chicken)
raw_recipe.description: This murgh makhani (Indian butter chicken) recipe is flavored with yogurt, tomato sauce, ginger, garlic, chili powder, garam masala, and fenugreek.

review.reviewBody: True to it's description, this is the "simple home version" that I have been looking for without the hassles of grinding cashews, grilling the chicken, etc, etc. The best decision I made was to follow the recipe exactly as it was written even down to the minutes for cooking each layer of ingredients, and that definitely paid off. The only substitution I made was using a tsp of frozen fenugreek leaves instead of dried, but I don't think that hurt it too much. Don't be deterred if you can't find the fenugreek leaves at all...I'm sure it's fine even without them. Will definitely be making this again for many years to come. Thanks so much for submitting this recipe! PS. One small note, if the chicken releases some water when initially browning it, dump it out of the pan before heating the remaining oil and browning the onions.

This was yummy, but I would recommend a couple things. Use heavy whipping cream instead of half and half. Or, condensed canned milk if you want a lighter dish. In India they never use half and half. For the "cooking oil," use vegetable oil. For the butter, you can make "ghee," which is cooked butter with removed fat. You cook the butter in a pan, and when you see the white coagulation on the top, strain the melted butter through a cheesecloth. You will have the golden goodness of the butter without the other stuff. It tastes nutty and flavorful, and if you're wondering what this stuff is - it's what you get with lobster at a good restaurant! You'll have to use a bit more butter (I use a pound) if you're going to make ghee. A lot will be removed in the straining process. Also, "tomato sauce" may be confusing. Don't use the stuff you use for pasta! (but that might be a big DUH). Use a can of pure tomatoes, diced or whole. Use the juice! And, one more thing. I tend to like more sauce with my rice and meat (I like to slurp it up with garlic naan and jasmine rice!) If you're like me, you'll want to use more heavy cream and yogurt. This will mean a pinch more of spices (careful with the chili powder!) Another tip - add yogurt to the dish slowly, so the rest of the sauce will "accept" it... the yogurt will curdle if too much is added at once. Happy eating!

Wow, this was a big hit! I did triple all ingredients and used cut-up boneless, skinless chicken breast. I cooked cut-up chicken breast in a non-stick dry grill pan and cooled. Then I marinated it in the yogurt/tandoori masala mixture in a plastic bag in the fridge. I reduced the oil used to about 1 tbsp. that I cooked the onion/ginger/garlic paste in. I was unable to find Indian chili powder and so I used regular chili powder which worked out just fine. Fabulous recipe, great instructions, easy to do.

I have made this several times now and it never disappoints. However, I do take two days to make it just because a) I usually have the time and b) It just takes it one notch up on the authentic ladder. I use boneless thighs that I cut into chunks and marinate overnight in a mixture of yogurt, onion, garlic and tandoori spice. The next day I thread the chunks onto BBQ skewers and grill them (you could also spread them on a greased baking sheet in the oven I would imagine) anyway, it gives the meat a slightly charred appearance and the tandoori flavor is amazing. I make the sauce by cooking the dry spices in a little ghee (or oil or butter) until fragrant (minute or two) then the rest of the ingredients. I’m also super crazy about cashews, so I do grind some up and add it as a thickening agent. Then the chicken comes off the skewers and into the sauce to simmer on low for awhile. I add the cream (or yogurt) at the very end. I even had to use a can of coconut milk once and it was fabulous as well. Oh, and I can’t get fresh fenugreek leaves so I use dried/ground and it’s absolutely fine. This recipe as written is amazing as is, but if you DO have the time to grill the chicken ahead with the tandoori flavors it is sooooo worth it!

I used this recipe mainly as a reference for the spices. I made it with lamb sprinkled with all the salt, garam masala, and tandoori masala - when the lamb was browned and all liquid evaporated, I added the ground ginger, onion, and garlic, and cooked for about 10 minutes. Then I added crushed tomatoes and cooked for about 45 minutes, until lamb was tender, then stirred in the cream. Really really good. Oh, and depending on the spiciness of your tandoori masala, the chili powder may not be necessary.

Loved this recipe. Made recipe as written except for fenugreek leaves. This is the third Butter Chicken recipe I’ve tried, but I’ve found a keeper. I liked the combinations of seasonings in this one, including the tandoori masala and homemade garlic/ginger paste (which I will do from now on). I used Indian chili powder and fenugreek seeds ground up (because I couldn’t find the leaves). Fenugreek is a must to make it take more authentic.

This was amazing & my husband claimed it was one of the best butter chicken recipes he has ever tasted. He loves Indian food, and says the best one he had was at an authentic restaurant in a big city but this one is runner up! 

I did make a few changes. I marinated the chicken in full fat greek yogurt (not nonfat yogurt) for 5 or 6 hours. I couldn't find fenugreek, so I omitted it. I used heavy whipping cream instead of half & half, and also added a couple tablespoons of tomato paste, and more chili powder. We had it with naan & rice. We will definitely be making this again!

Easy, quick, flavorful. I start with thighs with bones which are less expensive. I debone the thighs and use skin and bones to make stock while the chicken marinates. Then use the stock to make rice. Both garam masala and tandoori masala are easy to make with most ingredients from the spice cabinet.

Excellent! I doubled the sauce & didn't purée the onion, garlic & ginger as suggested, I just sautéed them together in the butter, but not the oil, then added the other ingredients. I only added about 1/3 teaspoon of salt, too. I also added 3 diced, cooked potatoes at the very end, because of the extra sauce. I usually use coconut milk instead of half and half. Wonderful dish, thank you for the recipe!

My family loved this recipe. I prepared it a bit differently, but flexibility is another plus for this recipe. I boiled bone-in chicken thighs, shredded the meat and added it to the sauce which I prepared separately. This lets me set aside plain meat for my toddlers, but lets the adults still eat what they want. I sauteed the onion/ginger/garlic puree in oil for several minutes, then sauteed in the spices, then added the yogurt and the cream. I added the chicken and let everything sit over low heat, covered, for about 40 minutes to let the flavors of the sauce and chicken exchange. It was great. I was able to find tomato sauce without seasoning so I did use tomato sauce, otherwise I would have used tomato puree.

This was AMAZING. My husband and I love Indian food, and this definitely compared to some of our local highly rated Indian restaurants'. I paired this with Aloo Palak (spinach and potatoes), and Basmati Rice and Naan on the side. I took the advice of previous reviews and added the heavy cream in lieu of half & half. My ONLY suggestion is -- double everything to yield a bigger batch. This reheats beautifully and travels well.

It was very delicious!, I had never tried Indian dishes before but I was interested to try it even though I do not have Tandoori Marsala powder and dried Fenugreek leaves however i decided to make spice blend of paprika, cumin, coriander and toasted Garam Marsala to give warm aromatic flavor of Indian dishes, I toast the spice blend in the skillet and actually add whole milk Greek yogurt and the toasted spice blend to the chicken and i actually refrigerate it overnight and the following day I'm ready to cook, I actually switch it to tomato condense soup instead of tomato sauce if I do not have one also, I cook the chicken for five minute and remove from the stove top before put it back to cook it again and it turns out beautiful, I serve it with homemade naan and white rice and I felt like i'm in the Indian restaurant! will make it again for sure!

This was great. I was excited to try making butter chicken from scratch instead of using the pre-made sauces. I didn’t have fenugreek so just used some dried herbs as suggested in one of the reviews. I also cut down the chili powder just because one of my children doesn’t do well with spice. Other than that I made as is and it was great. A bit more work than using the pre-made sauce, but easy enough if you have the prep time. Served with rice and garlic naan, and everyone enjoyed.
gorgeous curry - lovely flavours but not too hot or greasy
I started making this recipe about 10years ago and it's never failed. I find it better than a lot of the butter chicken take outs you find. Also freezes really well after cooking up a big batch.
So good! The only thing I would say is it’s a little spicy for me. I would half the cayenne. I also added peas after the rice was cooked to the rice as a vegetable.
Fabulous. I ran out of cream so used sour cream and it was terrific.

This is an amazing recipe! Thank you so much for sharing this! It tastes exactly like the butter chicken I bought at Trader Joe’s and even better! After having butter chicken for the first time, I have always wanted to cook it myself! And your recipe makes that possible.

I made this with broccoli, cauliflower, mushrooms, and carrots. Used more water and almond milk and fat free half and half. Used a little corn starch in the end to thicken the sauce. Served with jasmine rice. It turned out great!
